plan.major: Family Life and Human Development - Family Services Emphasis
plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-12 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Family Life and Human Development - Family Services Emphasis program page (poid=10825) and its linked official degree map, 'Family Life & Human Development Degree Maps (2026-2027)', tab 'Family Services (Campus)', last updated/reviewed August 3, 2026. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. Collected as the BS: the catalog prints a single combined Total Credits, BA/BS Degree: 120, and the map expressly states that students electing the BA take 16 credits of one foreign language, which are not included in the map. All courses must be passed with a C (2.0) or better to be counted in the major (catalog program information). This program requires completion of MATH 1040 - Statistical Inference (catalog program information); the map places it in Fall Year 1 at the catalog's 4 credits. Every semester's courses sum to the map's printed semester total (16/14/15/15/15/15/15/15) and the plan to the catalog's printed Total Credits, BA/BS Degree: 120. The catalog curriculum reconciles exactly: FLHD Core Requirements 30 (ten 3-credit courses, all placed on the map) plus Family Services Required Courses 22 (itemized 3+3+3+4+3+3+3, all placed) plus the Family Services Capstone 3 (one course, placed as a choice slot in Spring Year 4) plus Family Services Electives 9 (the map's three generic 3-credit elective rows, recorded as choice slots carrying the catalog's elective list) = the printed Curriculum of 64. The map's free rows total 37 credits (31 Free Electives + 6 Free Upper-division Electives), recorded as printed; the catalog prints no free-elective figure. GE and elective rows printed without course codes are recorded as choice slots with synthetic codes.
